subject: Post-analysis comparison of one species density between two habitats

messages.author: a8d314c9e9addfaa
messages.subject: Post-analysis comparison of one species density between two habitats
parts:
Hello everyone
Hope you all are staying healthy in this pandemic situation.
These days I am using the software Distance to analyse some data for training. The dataset contains observations of one species of bird and it is divided in two strata that correspond to two different habitats. 
I have read on one article that it is possible to use a Student's t-test "specific" procedure for a comparison of densities in the two habitats and that this procedure is described in Buckland et al.(1993) but I cannot find it there.
Does anyone know about this "specific procedure" described in Buckland et al.? Does anyone have another simple option?

Thank you all in advance for the attention

Greetings 

Dayron Lopez

Steve Buckland

messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Post-analysis comparison of one species density between two habitats
parts:
Dayron

If you are conversant in R, there is a function that performs tests of density estimates between two strata.  The code and demonstration of its use and interpretation can be found at

http://examples.distancesampling.org/differences/differences.html
